title: Close the DeviceRegistryDatabase connection on account_bootstrap.dart's exception path
why: `registry.close()` sits at the end of the try block, not in a finally. If sessionService.resolveActiveAccountId() (line 30) or registry.findById() (line 33) throws, execution jumps straight to the outer catch (line 51), which logs and returns a fallback filename WITHOUT ever closing the Drift-backed device_registry connection — the exact 'I/O fails halfway' scenario the Nygard lens asks about. Impact is low in practice (this runs once per app process at startup), but a leaked native database handle held for the app's whole lifetime is still an avoidable defect, and it would compound if this code path were ever retried (e.g. a future hot-reattempt) or re-used in a longer-lived context.
recommendation: Move `final registry = ...` construction above a try/finally (or wrap the resolveActiveAccountId/findById calls in try{...}finally{ await registry.close(); }) so every exit path closes the connection.
acceptance_criteria: registry.close() executes on both the success path and any exception path out of bootstrapAccount.
A unit test makes sessionService.resolveActiveAccountId() throw and asserts the registry/executor was still closed.
